{{Recipe}}

'''Tuwo shinkafa''' is a type of Nigerian [[Cookbook:Swallow|swallow]] made from mashed non-parboiled [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] or [[Cookbook:Corn|corn]]. It is mostly eaten by the Hausa in the northern part of the country. Tuwo shinkafa is usually prepared from scratch with short grain rice, but it can also be prepared with [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|rice flour]]. It is easy to prepare and usually serves as an accompaniment for [[Cookbook:Soup|soups]] and stews.

== Ingredients ==
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (2 [[Cookbook:Units of measurement#Nigeria|milk tin cups]]) short-grain non-parboiled [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]]
* [[Cookbook:Water|Water]] (about twice the volume of the rice)

== Equipment ==
*[[Cookbook:Stock Pot|Pot]]
*[[Cookbook: Potato Masher|Potato masher]] or wooden [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]]
*[[Cookbook: Mixing Bowl|Small container]] or wrapping nylon

== Procedure ==
# Wash the rice thoroughly, then drain.
# Add water to pot and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# Add the rinsed rice to the pot of boiling water.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] the rice until the water is absorbed and the rice is soft and sticky. If the rice hasn't softened when all the water is gone, add additional water as needed.
# Use the spatula to thoroughly mash the soft rice until it forms a soft [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Mold into desired container and allow to take shape of the container or wrap inside nylon
# Serve hot with your preferred [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

*Non-parboiled rice is preferred because it is more sticky
*Ensure thorough mashing to reduce rice lumps
